title: Bathroom Remodeling Advertising Ideas and Examples (2026)
summary: How bathroom remodelers advertise to get leads: real ad patterns, sample Google and Meta copy, channel picks and the math to set a budget.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Bathroom remodeling advertising works when it answers the buyer's fear of mess and downtime: a clear timeline, a clean job site, finished photos and a free consultation.
- The ads that stay live longest on the[bathroom remodeling ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/bathroom-remodeling-ads) lean on years in business, before and after proof, and a free design or quote.
- Best channels: Google Search, Google Business Profile and Facebook and Instagram video. Add Local Services Ads if your category is eligible.
- Measure cost per booked in-home consultation and close rate, not clicks.


## What live bathroom remodeling ads show


The[bathroom remodeling ads page](https://www.sprites.ai/bathroom-remodeling-ads) lists 51 live Meta ads from 12 advertisers. A few facts stand out.


- About 45% of the ads are video. Bathrooms are visual, and a before and after clip does work that a paragraph cannot.
- The median ad has been running 78 days. An ad that runs that long is usually one the advertiser has not needed to replace.
- The most common call to action is Learn more, on about 24% of ads. Most of the market sends people to a page first, not straight to a form.


The longest-running ads share a pattern. One has run for 1,706 days and opens by stating the company's 50+ years serving its area. Another, at 1,458 days, is a plain list of the remodeling services offered. A third opens with "44 years of experience in Bathroom Remodeling Contracting." A video ad that has run 490 days opens with "Before and after transformation." Another, at 419 days, leads with a free 3D design and custom quote.


None of these is clever. They state how long the company has been doing the work, show the result, and offer something free. That is a useful template, and it is easy to beat the many ads from generalist contractors that list every trade and say nothing specific about bathrooms.


## The bathroom buyer is worried about disruption


A bathroom is often the only one in the house. The homeowner is picturing a week without a shower, dust in the hallway and a crew that disappears. The price matters, but the fear of a messy, open-ended job often decides who gets the call. Your ad should name each worry and answer it.


Buyer worry What the ad should say Proof to show


How long will I be without a bathroom? State a realistic timeline for the job type, such as a tub to shower swap Dated project photos, a video walkthrough


Will my house be a mess? Mention floor protection, dust control and daily cleanup Photos of a protected hallway, a crew cleaning up


Can I trust this company? Years in business, license, insurance, local name Review count, license number


Will it look the way I imagine? Offer a free design consultation with visuals A 3D rendering next to the finished room


What will it cost? Give a starting range or a free quote A sample project with scope and price band


## Bathroom remodeling advertising examples


Below are sample lines you can adapt. Replace the town, timeline and numbers with your own, and only claim what you can deliver.


### Google Search ad


Responsive search ads allow up to 15 headlines of 30 characters and 4 descriptions of 90 characters, per Google Ads Help. A starter set for a remodeler in Austin:


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Bathroom Remodeler in Austin 28


Headline 2 Tub to Shower Conversions 25


Headline 3 Free 3D Design Consultation 27


Headline 4 Licensed, Insured, Local Crew 29


Description 1 We protect floors, seal off dust and clean up daily. Get a free quote with 3D design. 85


Description 2 Browse before and after photos and read our reviews. Book a free consultation. 78


Each headline should work alone, because Google combines them in different orders.


### Facebook and Instagram video ad


**Video:** 20 seconds, old tub on the left, new walk-in shower on the right, with a shot of the crew wiping down the floor at the end. **Primary text:** "Before and after of a hall bath in Round Rock. Four working days, floors protected, cleaned up every evening. Want to see yours in 3D before we start? Book a free design consultation." **Headline:** "Your new bathroom, without the mess." **Button:** Learn more or Get quote.


### Proof-first ad


"We have remodeled bathrooms in this county for 22 years. Licensed, insured, and one crew from demo to final walkthrough. See 30 finished bathrooms and get a free quote." This mirrors the years-in-business openings that have run longest on the wall.


### Accessibility and aging in place


"Walk-in showers, grab bars and non-slip floors, designed for your home. Free in-home consultation." A narrow offer for a specific buyer often beats a general one.


## Which channels work for a bathroom remodeler


1. **Google Search.** People searching "bathroom remodel near me" or "tub to shower conversion" are ready to talk. Build separate ad groups for each job type so the ad matches the search.
2. **Google Business Profile.** Post photos of finished bathrooms, collect reviews and keep hours current. It costs nothing and affects who gets the call.
3. **Facebook and Instagram.** Strong for video and for reaching homeowners before they search. Use finished work, a local offer and a lead form with questions on project type and timeline. The[Facebook ads for roofers](https://www.sprites.ai/facebook-ads-for-roofers) page shows how a neighboring trade structures these.
4. **Local Services Ads.** Pay-per-lead listings with a verified badge, available only in some categories and areas. Read the[Local Services Ads guide](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) and check Google's list for your trade.
5. **Referrals and yard signs.** Past clients and neighbors of a finished job are your cheapest leads. Put a sign up during the job and ask for a review at the final walkthrough.


If you also do plumbing work, the[plumbing marketing guide](https://www.sprites.ai/plumbing-marketing) covers the emergency side. For the wider picture, see[home services ads](https://www.sprites.ai/home-services-ads) .


## Turning bathroom remodeling leads into booked consultations


A lead is not a job. Most of the money in bathroom remodeling advertising is won or lost in the first day after the form is submitted.


- Call or text within 15 minutes during business hours. The homeowner has often filled out two or three forms.
- Ask three questions: what is the project, what is the timeline, and is there a budget range.
- Offer two specific consultation times instead of asking when they are free.
- Send a confirmation with the designer's name and photo, and a reminder the day before.


If your ads promise a free design visual, deliver it at the consultation. It gives the homeowner something to take home and compare.


## How to set a budget and measure results


Work backward from the job. This example uses assumed numbers, so replace them with yours.


Step Example


Monthly ad spend $2,000


Cost per lead $50, so 40 leads


Leads that book a consultation 40%, so 16 consultations


Consultations that sign 25%, so 4 jobs


Cost per signed job $2,000 / 4 = $500


Gross profit per job $15,000 average job at 30% = $4,500


In this example, each signed job costs $500 in ads and returns $4,500 in gross profit. If your close rate drops to 10%, cost per job rises to $1,250, which may still work. Track the numbers by channel each month, and cut the channel with the highest cost per signed job, not the one with the highest cost per click.

## FAQ


### What is the best bathroom remodeling advertising?


Google Search for people already looking, plus Facebook and Instagram video to show finished work. The ad should name the town, show a real before and after, state years in business, and offer a free consultation.


### How do I get bathroom remodeling leads?


Run Google Search ads on job types such as tub to shower conversions, keep a complete Google Business Profile, and use Meta lead ads with questions on project type and timeline. Then respond fast, because speed decides who books the consultation.


### Does video work for bathroom remodeling ads?


It appears to. About 45% of the live ads on the[ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/bathroom-remodeling-ads) are video, and one before and after video has run 490 days. Show the old room, the new room and the clean job site.


### How much should a bathroom remodeler spend on advertising?


Set it from the value of a signed job. Estimate your cost per lead, the share that book a consultation and the share that sign, then compare cost per signed job with gross profit per job. Spend more only where that math works.


### What should a bathroom remodeling ad say?


Lead with the job and the place, answer the fear of mess and downtime, add proof such as years in business or review count, and offer one next step, like a free design consultation or quote.
